standard: CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.5.NF.A.1 (adding fractions with unlike denominators; the mixed-number and subtraction parts of the standard are later missions)
source: Original content written for Pip, aligned to CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.5.NF.A.1. No textbook or published lesson was used.
attribution: None required (original content). The standard is cited by its code only.
in_scope: adding two fractions with unlike denominators, like 1/2 + 1/3
why pieces must be the same size before you can add them
equivalent fractions: the same amount cut into more pieces
finding a common denominator (any common multiple works, not only the smallest)
adding the numerators once the denominators match, and why the denominator stays
pizza, fraction bar and number line pictures
checking that an answer is reasonable (for example, 1/2 + 1/3 should be more than 1/2)
out_of_scope: mixed numbers and improper fractions (next mission)

look_fors: Says the pieces are different sizes (a half is bigger than a third)
Says you can only count pieces together when they are the same size, so 1/2 + 1/3 can't be added as they are
Backs it with a picture, object or example (pizza, bar, number line)

spoilers: the pieces have to be the same size
pieces must be the same size

concrete: what if i try to add a half pizza and a third pizza, how many slices is that?
connections: so it's like trying to add apples and oranges?

look_fors: Rewrites both fractions with the same denominator (for example 1/2 = 3/6 and 1/3 = 2/6)
Explains why that denominator works: both denominators go into it, so both fractions can be cut evenly into those pieces
Says the new fraction is the same amount as the old one, just cut into more pieces
probe_ladder: then how do i fix the pieces so i can add them?
would tenths work too, or only sixths?
can 6 slices make exactly a half? exactly a third?
then can i use fifths, because 2 + 3 = 5? that's what my rule says.
concepts.friend_nudge: My cousin said something about cutting both pizzas into same-size slices…? She didn't say what size.
concepts.aha: ok so you cut both into the same size slices
concrete: what if i cut both pizzas into 6 slices, how many slices is each fraction?
connections: so it's like cutting both pizzas into the same number of slices first?

look_fors: Adds only the numerators once the denominators match
Explains that the denominator names the size of the piece, so it stays the same (sixths plus sixths are still sixths)
Gets 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6, or checks that the answer is more than either fraction
probe_ladder: what do i do with 3/6 and 2/6 now?
what does the 6 on the bottom of 3/6 mean?
3 slices of a pizza cut in 6, plus 2 more slices. what size are my slices now?
then 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/12? that's what my rule says.
concepts.friend_nudge: My neighbor said the bottom number is like the name of the piece, like 'sixths'…? I'm not sure what she meant.
concepts.aha: so the bottom just says what size the slices are
concrete: what if i have 3 sixth-slices and 2 more, how many sixth-slices is that?
connections: so the bottom is like the name of the slice, like sixths?
